messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated error rate and 95th-percentile latency spike for tenant 'acme-corp' on dedicated-pool-42 (VPC eu-west-1) detected at 2026-02-12T14:30:01Z. Paging oncall: Jin (SRE)
Jin (SRE): Acked. Investigating. seeing 5xx rate ~18% and GPU utilization pinned at ~98% on pod set model-serving-v2. Starting live triage.
Jin (SRE): Quick checks: checking pod logs and metrics. `kubectl -n redwood get pods -l pool=dedicated-42 -o wide` returning many OOMKilled? Not OOMs but long GC pauses on runtime.
Alex W (SRE): Jumping in — I can take logs + traces. Any customer-facing outages yet?
Ryan (Customer Success): ACME reports slow responses and some requests timing out. They say production jobs stalled ~14:28 UTC. They're on a dedicated SLA and expect live updates.
Jin (SRE): Confirmed impact window 14:27-14:35 so far. All traffic to acme-corp routes through dedicated-pool-42 in eu-west-1. Looks like KV cache thrashing + Kernel driver spikes on GPU causing long tail latencies.
Eli (Eng-Platform): Noted. Quick mitigation options: 1) failover ACME to dedicated-pool-43 (compatible model bundle) 2) route ACME to hosted fallback (non-VPC) with strict data isolation agreement pending — needs CS signoff 3) scale up pool-42 (add nodes) — may take 3-6m.
Jin (SRE): Attempting scale up first (less customer-visible config change). Triggering autoscale override to +3 nodes.
Deploy Bot: Scaling request queued: pool=dedicated-42, change=+3 nodes, requested_by=Jin, request_id=scale-1775009001-1
Jin (SRE): Executed: `redwoodctl pools scale --pool dedicated-42 --delta 3 --reason "mitigate acme latency spike"`
Jin (SRE): While nodes are provisioning, I'm preparing to shift traffic to model-variant v2-slim (lower memory / quantized) on same pool if we keep seeing errors. That would reduce memory pressure.
Maria C (Oncall): Heads-up: my shift ends 14:45 UTC. If this goes beyond that, I'll hand off to Alex.
Alex W (SRE): Ready for handoff. If Jin needs to step out ping me and I'll take on-call.
Jin (SRE): Scale completed, nodes reporting Ready at 14:34:10 UTC. GPU util dropped to ~72% but 95th latency still elevated (~1.1s). Starting controlled reroute of acme traffic to v2-slim on dedicated-42. Using rollout command:
```
redwoodctl rollout create --target acme-corp --model v2-slim --traffic 25% --health-check 200,latency<800ms
```
Jin (SRE): Rolling at 25% -> monitoring.
Incident Bot: Deploy event: rollout-1775009001-2 triggered by Jin (SRE) at 2026-02-12T14:36:02Z
Jin (SRE): After 5 minutes, error rate dropped to ~2% and 95th latency ~420ms for traffic on v2-slim. Incrementing to 100% now.
Ryan (Customer Success): ACME says responses improving. They want an RCA and to know if credits apply under their Dedicated SLA.
Eli (Eng-Platform): Suggest we prepare a short exec update: root cause hypothesis (kernel/GPU memory fragmentation on model-serving-v2 under high KV churn), mitigation timeline, permanent fix options (quantized model baseline, memory leak hunt, better cache eviction), and recommended SLA credit (per contract).
Jin (SRE): Creating timeline note for RCA draft. Preliminary timeline: detection 14:30, paging 14:30, scale request 14:31, nodes ready 14:34, gradual rollout 14:36, full recovery 14:41.
Alex W (SRE): I'll capture the logs and attach key stack traces to the RCA doc. Pointing to internal log slices: `s3://redwood-logs/incidents/1775009001/*.log`
Ryan (Customer Success): Please include user-visible impact: ~14:27-14:41, intermittent timeouts for batch jobs and synchronous API calls, estimated affected requests ~1.8k. CS will draft comms to ACME with proposed credit and timeline.
Eli (Eng-Platform): Proposed fix steps for postmortem: 1) pin acme-corp to v2-slim until kernel/driver fix validated 2) backport quantization and reduce KV cache footprint 3) add eviction policy improvements and mem usage alerting 4) run stress tests that mirror ACME traffic patterns in staging dedicated pools 5) consider dedicated hot spare nodes for critical tenants
Maria C (Oncall): Handing off to Alex — I'm signing out now. Alex, I'm available by DM for 15m. :wave:
Alex W (SRE): Taking over oncall. Noted open action items: finalize RCA draft, coordinate with CS for credit calc, schedule follow-up with Platform and ML infra.
Jin (SRE): Thanks Maria. I'll continue analysis for root cause — focusing on recent driver update that landed 3 days ago.
Deploy Bot: Rollout event completed: rollout-1775009001-2 by Jin -> success at 2026-02-12T14:41:03Z
Alex W (SRE): Drafting a short post-incident summary for ACME and execs. Draft (internal):
"At 14:30 UTC we observed sustained latency and elevated 5xxs for ACME on their dedicated pool caused by excessive memory churn on model-serving-v2 after a recent driver/kernel interaction under high KV churn. Immediate mitigations: scaled pool capacity (+3 nodes) and rolled ACME to a lower-memory model variant (v2-slim), restoring service by 14:41 UTC. Next steps: rollback driver test, memory profiling, model quantization, and improved mem alerts. Proposed SLA credit: one week of reserved-capacity credit (per SLA section 4.2)."
Alex W (SRE): Feedback welcome — flagging Eli and Ryan for approval on wording and proposed credit.
Ryan (Customer Success): That wording looks good. I'll prepare the customer-facing message and include the credit proposal. Will send for legal review.
Eli (Eng-Platform): Approve wording. For timeline we should add the exact node IDs and traces. I'll add those to the RCA.
Jin (SRE): Adding diagnostic notes: GPUs were showing repeated driver context resets on 3 pods (ids p-9a3, p-9b1, p-9c7). Kernel logs attached in RCA. Also note an increase in KV miss rate correlated with long sequences from ACME batch jobs.
Alex W (SRE): Action items (assign): Jin -> deep driver/kernel debugging + reproduce in staging by Tue 2026-02-17; Eli -> add mem alerts and eviction policy by Fri 2026-02-20; Ryan -> customer comms + SLA credit coordination today; Alex -> finalize RCA and exec summary tomorrow EOD.
Incident Bot: Incident 1775009001 marked: RESOLVED at 2026-02-12T14:41:05Z by Jin (SRE)
Ryan (Customer Success): ACME acknowledged and appreciated the rapid updates. They're requesting a follow-up meeting with engineering to discuss long-term mitigations next week. I'll schedule once we have RCA draft.
Alex W (SRE): Draft RCA link (internal): https://redwood.internal/docs/incidents/1775009001-rca (please comment)
Jin (SRE): Adding final note — we recommended keeping ACME on v2-slim for 2 weeks while we validate kernel fix in staging.
Eli (Eng-Platform): I'll create a runbook change to include fallback model rollout steps for dedicated tenants and a checklist for scale overrides.
Ryan (Customer Success): Thanks team. I'll confirm credit amount after legal, update ACME, and include exec note for their CTO.
Alex W (SRE): Closing thread for now. If anyone discovers further telemetry that changes root cause, reopen or ping me. :white_check_mark:
